mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the cost of capital declines.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based demand contraction, causing a negative earnings outlook and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., when both series decline, returns are positive in >55% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0), supply chain disruptions intensify, leading to higher input costs and reduced corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% year-over-year) signals an inflationary environment that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation (measured by PAYEMS growth) indicates improving economic conditions and higher corporate hiring, which supports earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong aggregate demand, boosting corporate revenues and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., when both series increase, returns are negative in >55% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 110.0) indicates a weakening supply sector, which reduces corporate output and profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is below 110.0.
